q: Name the two grands crus whose delimited area straddles the boundary between Puligny-Montrachet and Chassagne-Montrachet.
exp: Montrachet and Bâtard-Montrachet straddle the border; Chevalier and Bienvenues lie wholly in Puligny, Criots wholly in Chassagne.

q: Which Gevrey-Chambertin grand cru may legally label as either 'Charmes-Chambertin' or 'Mazoyères-Chambertin'?
accept: mazoyeres may be sold as charmes
exp: Mazoyères may take the Charmes name — nearly all producers do; the reverse is not permitted.

q: Give the two monopole grands crus owned entirely by Domaine de la Romanée-Conti.
exp: Six others are shared; these two are DRC's alone.

q: La Romanée, at ~0.85 ha the smallest AOP in France, is the monopole of which domaine?
exp: Vosne-Romanée's tiniest grand cru sits directly above Romanée-Conti.

q: Which Chablis grand cru climat is generally considered the greatest and largest of the seven?
exp: Les Clos: ~26 ha, the fullest and longest-lived. The seven share one slope with La Moutonne as an honorary eighth.

q: Name the négociant house whose monopole La Moutonne overlaps Vaudésir and Preuses.
exp: La Moutonne is an unofficial grand cru; the INAO tolerates the label.

q: Which village's premiers crus include Les Amoureuses and Les Charmes?
exp: Les Amoureuses, below Musigny, trades at grand cru prices.

q: Name Vosne-Romanée's three premiers crus most often cited as grand-cru quality (any two).
ans: e.g., Cros Parantoux, Aux Malconsorts, Les Beaux Monts (also Les Suchots, Aux Brûlées)
exp: Henri Jayer made Cros Parantoux immortal.

q: The hill of Corton's white grand cru, Corton-Charlemagne, spans which three villages?
exp: Legend says Charlemagne's queen tired of red-stained beards — hence the white.

q: What is a 'climat' in Burgundian usage?
accept: specific named site with its own identity
~a named, delimited vineyard site with its own terroir identity
ans: A named, delimited vineyard site with its own terroir identity
exp: UNESCO listed the climats of the Côte d'Or in 2015; 'lieu-dit' is the cadastral name, 'climat' the wine identity.

q: Which Morey-Saint-Denis grand cru is the commune's second-largest and a near-monopole of Domaine des Lambrays?
exp: Clos de Tart, its neighbor, is a true monopole — held by Mommessin for a century, now Pinault's Artémis. Morey's smallest grand cru is Clos Saint-Denis (~6.6 ha).

q: Clos de Tart, a grand cru monopole of Morey-Saint-Denis, was founded by which order?
exp: The nuns of Tart-le-Haut held it from 1141 until the Revolution.

q: What does 'Tastevinage' signify on a Burgundy label?
accept: approved by the confrerie des chevaliers du tastevin
selected in blind tasting by the confrerie
ans: Selection in blind tasting by the Confrérie des Chevaliers du Tastevin (Clos de Vougeot)
exp: A marketing imprimatur, not an INAO classification.

q: Give the maximum base yield (rendement de base) for red grand cru Burgundy, within 5 hl/ha.
exp: Village reds run ~40-45; the pyramid narrows yields as it rises.

q: Which premier cru of Volnay, the monopole of Domaine Marquis d'Angerville, is often called grand-cru-in-waiting?
exp: Volnay and Pommard have no grands crus; Clos des Ducs, Taillepieds and Caillerets argue the case.

q: Pommard's two most celebrated premiers crus are:
exp: Rugiens (iron-rich, muscular) and Epenots (silkier) headline any future grand-cru promotion.
